screens.heading: You are safe here
screens.reassurance: This module will not send anything to any AI service. You are just reading.
screens.goal: By the end of this module, you will know how to use AI tools to research health questions, get plain-language explanations, write helpful messages, and protect your privacy while doing so.

screens.heading: What AI is good at — and what it is not
body: AI is excellent at explaining things in plain language, summarising complex documents, generating ideas, and answering general questions about topics that are well-established.

AI is not a substitute for professional advice. It does not know your medical history, your other medications, your specific circumstances, or the latest breaking news. It can get facts wrong — confidently.
The right approach: use AI as a starting point to understand something, then verify important information with a professional (your doctor, pharmacist, lawyer, or financial adviser).
screens.tellMeMore: AI tools that are safe and free to use: Claude (claude.ai) from Anthropic, ChatGPT (chat.openai.com) from OpenAI, and Gemini (gemini.google.com) from Google. All three are available in a web browser or app. You do not need to create an account to try Claude — just visit the website and start typing.

screens.heading: Using AI for health questions safely
body: AI is genuinely useful for understanding health topics in plain language. Good examples: 'What are the general side effects of metformin?' or 'Can you explain what a herniated disc is in simple terms?' or 'What questions should I ask my doctor before starting a new blood pressure medication?'

After getting an AI answer, verify it with your pharmacist (free, in person or by phone) or your doctor. Pharmacists at any Canadian drugstore can answer medication questions for free — no appointment needed.
Never share your full name, OHIP number, SIN, or specific medical history with any AI tool. Ask general questions — you get the same useful information without the privacy risk.
screens.tellMeMore: The golden rule for AI privacy: before typing anything, ask yourself — 'Would I be comfortable if this was posted on a community bulletin board?' Instead of 'I take 10mg of metformin and my doctor is Dr. Smith,' type: 'What are the general side effects of metformin?' The answer is just as useful — without your personal details attached.

screens.heading: Practical things to try right now
body: AI is useful for everyday tasks that have nothing to do with technology: 'Write a birthday card message for my brother who loves fishing and turns 70 this week.' 'What are good indoor plants for a sunny Ontario apartment that are hard to kill?' 'Help me write an email to my landlord asking about a repair that has not been fixed.'

For Canadian-specific questions: 'What is the difference between RRSP and TFSA in Canada?' or 'What day trips are good from London, Ontario for someone who loves history?' AI handles these well — just verify financial information with your bank.
For translation: 'Translate this into French: How do I get to the pharmacy?' Or paste a foreign-language document and ask for a summary in English.
screens.tellMeMore: You can also use AI to help you prepare for a doctor's appointment: 'I have an appointment about my knee pain. What questions should I ask?' AI will generate a list of questions — bring it with you. This is one of the most practical and immediately useful things AI can do for healthcare, and it does not require sharing any personal information.

screens.heading: When AI is not enough — call a professional
body: Use AI for general understanding. Call a professional for: any new or worsening symptom; stopping or changing a medication; chest pain, trouble breathing, sudden confusion, or severe pain (call 911); deciding whether a supplement or treatment is right for your specific situation.
Telehealth Ontario (1-866-797-0000): free 24/7 nurse line — always the right call when you are unsure whether something needs medical attention.
Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (1-888-495-8501): if AI-generated content was used to scam you, or if you are unsure whether a message or website is legitimate.
screens.tellMeMore: AI cannot replace your pharmacist. A Canadian pharmacist can review all your medications for dangerous interactions, answer questions about dosing and side effects, advise on over-the-counter remedies, and refer you to a doctor when needed — all for free, with no appointment, simply by walking in or calling. This is one of Canada's most underused healthcare resources.

screens.heading: AI is your research assistant — not your doctor
takeaways: Use AI for plain-language explanations, general questions, writing help, and research starting points.
Never share your OHIP number, SIN, full address, or specific medical details with any AI tool.
Golden rule: ask general questions ('what are the side effects of X?') not personal ones ('I am taking X — is it safe for me?').
Verify important health information with your pharmacist (free, no appointment) or doctor.
Telehealth Ontario (1-866-797-0000): free 24/7 nurse line for health concerns that need a real professional.
screens.confidence: You can now use AI to get clear answers to health questions, write helpful messages, and research almost anything — safely and with your privacy protected.
